title: The lookup table that rides on every read
impact: Performance: accepted, and the mechanism is a cache that was never as free as it looked. `RowSchema` built its name-to-index `HashMap` in its constructor. A worker caches one schema per SQL, so it was built once — but the schema travels with every result and `SendPort.send` copies the graph it is handed, and a `HashMap` copies as one object per entry. Every `select()` in the library therefore shipped a lookup table most results never consult. Measured with no database and one echo isolate, the map is worth 0.30 us of hop at six columns, 1.17 us at 21 and 1.79 us at 40, while the column-name list it is built from costs nothing measurable at any width — strings cross a same-group boundary by reference, so the whole schema-transfer cost was the index. Building it on first use costs 95/322/617 ns at the same widths, once per result set and only when a caller supplies a key the identity scan misses. End to end, across three order-flipped collections of two AOT bundles from separate worktrees: a 40-column read -22.4% and a 21-column one -12.1% in every pass, point reads negative in all six passes at a collection floor the two zero-ceiling controls put at -10% to +29%, and a 1,000-row result consumed entirely by column name unchanged at -0.5% — 6,000 lookups against one build, which is where the per-read saving and the per-lookup tax cancel. Two things had to be right to get there: the build lives in a `vm:never-inline` sibling, because the natural `??=` form cost the steady-state probe enough to read +1.1%/+4.0% on that same lane, and the field is typed as the concrete `HashMap`. Along the way the run measured what exp 176 had only stated — the identity fast path never fires for a source literal, because decoded column names are never canonicalized — and corrected a doc comment that claimed the opposite. One nullable field and one out-of-line method in `lib/src/row.dart`; no public API change; `resultSetHasNameIndex` plus a test pin the negative property that a delivered result carries no index.
